QF.id: XVI Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_32

question.text: Replacement cost risk in commodity derivatives refers to:

answer.text: The cost of replacing a defaulted trade at current — and possibly adverse — market prices, a pre-settlement risk
The cost of replacing damaged goods in a warehouse
The cost of switching from one broker to another

explanation.text: The Logic: Replacement cost risk is the risk of having to replace a defaulted trade at the prevailing market price, which may have moved adversely since the original trade. It is a pre-settlement risk borne while the trade is still outstanding. The Trap: Novation through the clearing corporation eliminates principal risk by interposing the CC as counterparty — it does not, by itself, eliminate replacement cost risk. Replacement cost exposure is instead contained by mark-to-market settlement and margin requirements. Note: Daily MTM limits one party's accumulated mark-to-market exposure to roughly a single day's price movement, which is why disciplined MTM collection is central to managing replacement cost risk.
